intent: Change one thing: widen the row from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m at 16 mm, five sensors at 0.02 m spacing, y = 0.04, with the Integrator's kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller. This isolates the widening from the gain change that confounded iteration 4. I expect line loss to fall below 1.0 per run and s-bend progress to exceed 0.210, because the coverage edge moves to about 0.0605 m. I expect no completion yet. If line loss stays at 1.0 or more, I will test a 12 mm footprint at the same ±0.04 m spacing next. I am not committing to a forward offset.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) if ±0.04 m at kp 1.2 gives line loss below 1.0 and s-bend progress above 0.210, the wider coverage edge was helping and iteration 4's drop was the gain. (2) If line loss stays at 1.0 or more, 16 mm edge noise or the shallower steering slope is the cause, and the 12 mm footprint at ±0.04 m is the discriminator. (3) If the loss occurs near progress 0, it is start-up or entry gain, not coverage, and the geometry should be held. Please report the progress at the first line-loss event on each track and the max error at that moment.
rationale: Iteration 7 held the best-raced geometry (±0.03 m, 16 mm, y = 0.04). Its controller restore is confirmed at 69.46 (iterations 3, 5, 6, 7 all match), so the simulator is deterministic for this layout and the 0.06 m off-track limit is the binding failure. Max error sits near 0.062 m on every track, and line loss stays at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run. Iteration 4 changed the row to ±0.04 m and kp to 1.0 together, and the score fell to 61.49. The Integrator's feedback reads that as mainly a gain effect, and I agree the widening was never tested alone. The Integrator has restored kp 1.2 and kd 0.4 and asked for the ±0.04 m row at 16 mm, y = 0.04, at that gain. I am taking that advice now, because it is the one untested geometry question and the controller is already tuned for a row of this kind. The outer footprint edge reaches about 0.0605 m offset (0.0125 + 0.008 + 0.04), against about 0.0505 m for ±0.03 m, which should move coverage loss to the limit itself. Wheels, body and mass are unchanged, so any change in score comes from the row alone. I expect progress above 0.21 on the s-bend with line loss below 1.0 if coverage was the limit. If line loss stays at 1.0 or more, the next test is a 12 mm footprint at the same spacing, to check for 16 mm edge noise. I am not moving the row forward, because slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.145 to 0.147, below the 0.15 trigger.
